title: Capstone: Stateless Tool Ecosystem
service: ResearchOps: the capstone's research-and-report system in process: an agent that discovers a simulated research MCP server and calls it through a scope-checking gateway with fresh _meta on every request, delegates summaries to a writer agent over A2A, polls the report task with tasks/get and keeps in-memory spans; a CSV paper fixture; a research job under hard limits; a Markdown report streamed in paper order; and a claim graph that decides what a run proves
deviations: Part 1, defect 2: the suggestion hung the A2A delegation span under the root instead of under the tool span that issued it. In this exam the agent itself delegates the summaries, as in the lesson's Target trace (agent.invoke_agent --> A2A SendMessage), because Part 3 needs the delegations on the client side (delegation budget, missing papers), so a SendMessage span under the root is correct here. The planted parentage defect is the other edge the Target trace draws: tasks/get polls hung under the root instead of under the tools/call generate_report span that returned the handle.

Part 1, defect 1: the server refuses the undeclared tools/call itself, as the lesson says it must, so the -32021 cannot come from a tasks/get; it is raised one call later, in the polling step (_settle), which is where the candidate first looks at the polls' _meta.

Part 1, defect 3: generate_report needs research:read and research:write (the lesson's table names research:write only), so that 'any scope' and 'every scope' give different answers; a write-only token closes the 'check write alone' fix.

Part 1, defect 4: the 20 polls wait 40, 80 and then 40 ms again (1.08 s of sleeping) instead of 20 x 50 ms, so the overfix guard also catches waits that never get shorter. The guard requires every wait to equal the server's current pollIntervalMs, which is both 'not less than the current interval' and 'follows the server's changes'.

Part 3: no resources/read of the ui:// resource. The lesson says only that the completed task's final result contains text and a ui:// reference, and Lesson 14 gates resources/read of a UI behind the Apps extension, so the job returns the final result with its ui:// reference instead of inventing that call.

Part 3: 'total polling time' is the client's own budget.wait_ms, kept separate from the ttlMs backstop; ttl counts from when the handle arrived, on the agent's clock (Lesson 13: ttlMs is measured from creation and a client can treat it as a backstop). The retry that counts against the tool-call budget is one retry of a tools/call answered with isError: true.
The simulated server also answers tasks/cancel with an acknowledgement (Lesson 13's shape), so a job that cancels when it gives up is not punished; the tests do not require it.

Part 4: the summaries arrive as an async iterator of Summary(arxiv_id, text or None), so the part does not depend on Part 3. One trap is added: whitespace in titles is folded to single spaces, because arXiv titles carry line breaks (Part 2's fixture has them) and a heading must stay on one line.

Part 5: trace-parent evidence is computed from the spans the collector received (Use It step 6: assert parentage at the receiver), not taken from an evidence item, so the 'shared trace id' trap lives in code. Evidence names come from the Required evidence column of the Simulation versus production table.

parts.lesson_anchor: Stateless MCP changes the integration boundary (advertise io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks in the same request that may receive a task handle, or the server returns -32021 with requiredCapabilities); Target trace (tools/call: generate_report --> tasks/get polling; a shared trace identifier alone does not prove correct parentage); Security posture (gateway RBAC that checks the requested tool and scope); Exercise 4 (respect pollIntervalMs); code/main.py orchestrator, gateway_call and tasks_get
planted_bugs: Agent.request declares the Tasks extension only for tasks/* methods, so the tools/call for generate_report gets -32021; the ProtocolError surfaces one call later, in _settle, the polling step, before any tasks/get was sent
call_tool hands _settle the caller's span instead of its own, so the 20 tasks/get spans hang under agent.invoke_agent; every span still shares one trace id
Gateway.handle lets a call through when the token holds any of the required scopes (required & grant.scopes), so a research:read token can call generate_report
_settle waits with time.sleep instead of the injected self.sleep, blocking the event loop and taking about 1.2 s for 20 polls
parts.timing_assert: a research run with 20 polls (7 x 40, 7 x 80, 6 x 40 ms) under 0.1 s with the injected sleep. Measured on this machine under load (load average 5 to 8): the time.sleep version 1.15 to 1.28 s (11x the limit or more); the fixed version 0.49 ms median, 1.2 ms at p99 and 5.6 ms at worst over 2000 runs (17x under the limit or more), with one scheduling spike of 32.7 ms in 1200 earlier runs
parts.overfix_guard: every wait must equal the server's current pollIntervalMs while the interval goes 40 -> 80 -> 40 ms, so removing the wait, keeping the handle's interval, never waiting less than before, passing milliseconds, polling before the first wait and a sleep that is never awaited all fail; asyncio.sleep and asyncio.to_thread(time.sleep) still take wall-clock time; polling once, as code/main.py does, raises TaskFailed; the server must still refuse an undeclared generate_report with -32021 and the lesson's requiredCapabilities, so deleting its check fails; declaring the extension for generate_report only fails the every-tools/call check; a write-only token closes the 'check write alone' fix; a refused call must not reach the server and must be audited

parts.lesson_anchor: Target architecture and Target trace (server/discover, arxiv_search, A2A SendMessage, generate_report as a task, tasks/get polling, completed task with the final result and a ui:// reference); Exercise 4 (respect pollIntervalMs, read the final result without tasks/result); Use It step 3 (timeout and TTL; do not add tasks/result); Simulation versus production: Delegation (timeout and retry tests); The Concept: production tests must exercise timeouts and retries
traps: a retry not counted against budget.tool_calls, or sent without a budget check (budgets 1 and 2)
retrying until the budget runs out instead of once
delegations awaited one at a time (the writer records its peak concurrency)
gather without return_exceptions or a TaskGroup: one DelegationFailed fails the job
return_exceptions=True with the exception kept as a summary
hits past budget.delegations delegated, or not counted as missing
summaries in completion order (as_completed) instead of search order
missing left out of the generate_report arguments
tasks/result called after completion (-32601)
no ttl backstop, ttl compared in seconds or with >, counted from the start of the job, checked against the end of the next wait, or checked after the wait budget
the wait budget checked after waiting, with >=, read off the clock, or missing (649, 650 and 700 ms budgets)
the handle's pollIntervalMs kept for every poll
parts.integration: runs on Part 1's Agent (request, get_task, delegate, sleep, clock) through the gateway and the simulated server, with a scripted writer agent that spends fake time
clarifying_questions: whether server/discover counts as a tool call

parts.lesson_anchor: The Problem (the system delegates summarization and generates a report); Target trace (delegated work finishes independently); Key Terms: Opacity boundary (the caller sees only the returned artifacts)
parts.wire_format: Markdown text; the test joins the chunks and splits them at CommonMark ATX headings (up to three spaces, one to six #, then a space or the end of the line), and records how many summaries had been pulled when each heading went out
traps: summaries not escaped, only lines that start exactly with # escaped, or every # escaped
sections in arrival order
everything held until the stream ends, or every summary read first
the search results sent only with the first summary
one buffered section released per summary instead of every section that is ready
failed or never-arrived papers left out, not counted as missing in the conclusion, or listed there in arrival order
titles with line breaks written as they are, or with only the line breaks replaced
sections glued together without a line break
a plain async function instead of an async generator
clarifying_questions: a summary for an unknown paper

parts.lesson_anchor: Simulation versus production (the Required evidence column; a green local run validates the simulation only); Target trace (a shared trace identifier alone does not prove correct parentage, export, or backend ingestion); Use It step 6 (export spans to a test collector and assert parentage at the receiver); Exercise 1; Key Terms: Integration evidence
